title: Immunofluorescence staining of phosphoinositides in primary mouse hippocampal neurons in dissociated culture
protocol: Soak coverslips in cleaning solution for 12–16 hours or longer in 150 mm glass petri plates on a flat rotator.
Remove cleaning solution and rinse coverslips sequentially with distilled water (dH₂O) and double distilled water (ddH₂O).
Change water every 30 minutes or longer during rinsing.
Rinse coverslips twice with absolute alcohol for 1 hour or longer on a flat rotator.
Autoclave sterilize the coverslips in a 90 mm glass petri dish.
Add coverslips into a 24-well cell culture plate, one coverslip per well.
Coat coverslips with 300 μL PDL solution (0.1 mg/mL) for at least 2 hours before culturing primary neurons.
Sterilize surgical instruments by ultraviolet light irradiation or soaking in 75% ethanol for more than 20 min.
Air dry sterilized instruments in a tissue culture hood before use.
Add 15 mL of dissection buffer to a sterile 100 mm cell culture petri dish.
Add 1 mL of dissection buffer to a 1.5 mL sterile Eppendorf tube.
Keep the 1.5 mL sterile Eppendorf tube with dissection buffer on ice.
Sanitize P0 C57BL/6J mouse by quick immersion in 75% ethanol.
Transfer the pup to a sterile petri dish.
Decapitate the mouse quickly with sharp straight delicate scissors.
Fix the head with straight ophthalmic forceps.
Cut the skull along the medulla oblongata with mayo spring scissors.
Dissect out the mouse brain and transfer it to precooled dissection buffer in 100 mm petri dish.
Remove the olfactory bulb and epencephalon from the brain.
Strip away meninges under a dissecting microscope using fine smooth forceps.
Reverse the brain and fix it gently on the periphery of the cortex with fine forceps.
Cut off one hippocampus from the cortex, clear up the meninges, and remove extra tissue.
Isolate the other hippocampus from the contralateral side of the cortex.
Transfer hippocampi to a precooled dissection buffer in 1.5 mL sterile Eppendorf tubes.
Place the tube on ice until all hippocampi are collected.
Put no more than six hippocampi in one tube, transfer to a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube if necessary.
Remove the dissection buffer and add 0.25% trypsin (use 1.5 mL for ≤6 hippocampi, 2-5 mL for >6 hippocampi).
Keep the tube in a humidified incubator at 5% CO2 and 37°C for 15–17 minutes.
Gently reverse the centrifuge tube 3–4 times every 5 minutes.
Aspirate off PDL from coverslips.
Add 500 μL autoclaved ddH2O to wells.
Shake the plate gently.
Keep coverslips in water for 5 min or shorter.
Repeat step of adding and shaking water at least twice.
Aspirate off water.
Position coverslips in the center of wells.
Let coverslips air dry for less than 10 min in the hood.
Remove 0.25% trypsin from hippocampi.
Rinse hippocampi with equal volume of DMEM culture medium by reversing the tube 6–8 times gently.
Let hippocampi stand for 3 min at 21°C–25°C or until they settle at the bottom.
Remove the culture medium.
Repeat rinsing of hippocampi twice with DMEM culture medium.
Add 0.5 mL DMEM culture medium to hippocampi in a fresh 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Gently triturate the hippocampal tissue 8 times with P1000 pipette.
Let the tube stand still for ∼3 min.
Transfer the supernatant (dissociated cells in suspension) to a fresh 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 0.5 mL DMEM culture medium to the pellet from step 21.
Gently triturate with P1000 pipette for 8 times to dissociate more cells.
Let the tube stand still for ∼3 min.
Collect the supernatant and discard the pellet.
Combine the supernatants (cell suspensions) collected from steps 20 and 21.
Count the number of cells in suspension with a hemocytometer.
If the cell suspension is too diluted, concentrate by centrifugation at 300×g for 10 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in appropriate volume of DMEM culture medium.
Add hippocampal neurons in 60–70 μL DMEM culture medium on air-dried PDL-coated coverslip carefully at a density of 2–3×10^4 cells/well.
Keep the tissue culture plate in humidified incubator (5% CO2, 37°C) for 5–10 min.
Add 450 μL DMEM culture medium into each well and incubate in humidified incubator (5% CO2, 37°C) for 4 h.
Replace DMEM with 500 μL Neurobasal-A culture medium pre-warmed to 37°C.
Replenish the dissociated culture by adding 500 μL of fresh Neurobasal-A culture medium to each well on Day 3 in vitro (DIV3) and every three days afterward.
Dilute 0.5 μg DNA in 50 μL Neurobasal-A Medium.
Add 0.5 μL PLUS™ Reagent to the diluted DNA and mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Incubate the mixture of diluted DNA and PLUS™ Reagent for 5 min at 21°C–25°C.
Dilute 1 μL Lipofectamine® LTX Reagent in 50 μL Neurobasal-A Medium and mix gently.
Incubate the diluted Lipofectamine® LTX Reagent for 5 min at 21°C–25°C.
Add the mixture of diluted DNA and PLUS™ Reagent to the diluted Lipofectamine® LTX Reagent and mix gently.
Incubate the combined solution for 20 min at 21°C–25°C.
Replace the culture medium in each well of the 24-well culture plate with 400 μL Neurobasal-A Medium (pre-warmed to 37°C).
Add the DNA-lipid complex to neurons cultured in a 24-well culture plate drop by drop.
Shake the plate gently back and forth to uniformly disperse the DNA-lipid complex.
Incubate neurons for 50–60 min at 37°C.
Replace the DNA-lipid complex with culture medium (mixture of old and fresh Neurobasal-A culture medium, with fresh medium accounting for 1/3–1/2 of the total volume).
Incubate neurons at 37°C in a CO2 incubator for 72 h or longer to express mCherry in neurons as a morphological marker.
Do gently mix the Lipofectamine® LTX Reagent and Lipofectamine PLUS™ Reagent in their original tubes before use.
Fix neurons in 200 μL medium by adding 200 μL PBS containing 4% FA (pre-warmed to 21°C–25°C) along the sidewall of the culture plate, and incubate for 15 min at 21°C–25°C.
Remove buffer or medium from neurons.
Fix neurons rapidly by adding 400 μL PBS containing 2% FA and 4% sucrose (pre-warmed to 21°C–25°C) along the sidewall of the culture plate, and incubate for 15 min at 21°C–25°C.
Rinse neurons three times with PBS containing 50 mM NH4Cl, 5 min each.
Permeabilize neurons with buffer A containing 25 μg/mL digitonin for 5–10 min.
Rinse neurons immediately for three times with buffer A, 5 min each.
Block neurons with buffer A containing 5% (v/v) NGS and 50 mM NH4Cl for 45 min.
Rinse neurons once with buffer A.
Incubate neurons with primary antibodies in buffer A containing 5% NGS for 1 h.
Rinse neurons for three times with buffer A, 5 min each.
Incubate neurons with secondary antibodies in buffer A containing 5% NGS for 45 min away from light.
Rinse neurons for three times with buffer A, 5 min each.
Postfix neurons with 2% FA in PBS for 5 min.
Rinse neurons for three times with PBS containing 50 mM NH4Cl to remove the residual FA.
Incubate neurons with PBS containing DAPI for 5 min.
Mount coverslips on glass slide with mounting medium after one rinse with PBS and then with distilled ddH2O.
Do not move the coverslips during fixation.
Handle the coverslips gently when rinsing cells or aspirating liquid to preserve neuron integrity.
Avoid excessive permeabilization to prevent severe loss of signals.
Costain intracellular PIP (PI3P, PI4P or PI(4,5)P2) and Rab8 (protein marker for secretory endosome).
Costain intracellular PIP (PI3P, PI4P or PI(4,5)P2) and TGN46 (protein marker for the trans-Golgi network).
Detect intracellular PIPs and Rab8/TGN46 using the intracellular staining procedure.
Fix mouse hippocampal neurons on DIV12.
Co-immunostain fixed mouse hippocampal neurons for intracellular PI3P and Rab8.
Co-immunostain fixed mouse hippocampal neurons for intracellular PI4P and Rab8.
Co-immunostain fixed mouse hippocampal neurons for intracellular PI(4,5)P2 and Rab8.
Co-immunostain fixed mouse hippocampal neurons for intracellular PI3P and TGN46.
Co-immunostain fixed mouse hippocampal neurons for intracellular PI4P and TGN46.
Co-immunostain fixed mouse hippocampal neurons for intracellular PI(4,5)P2 and TGN46.
Fix neurons rapidly in 200 μL medium by adding 200 μL PBS containing 8% FA and 0.4% GA (pre-warmed to 21°C–25°C) along the sidewall of the culture plate for 15 min at 21°C–25°C.
Remove buffer or medium and fix neurons rapidly with 400 μL PBS containing 4% FA, 0.2% GA and 4% sucrose (pre-warmed to 21°C–25°C) along the sidewall of the culture plate for 15 min at 21°C–25°C.
Rinse neurons three times with PBS containing 50 mM NH4Cl at 21°C–25°C, 5 min each.
Place coverslips in ice bath for 4 min to pre-chill samples before blocking.
Block neurons with buffer A containing 5% (v/v) NGS, 50 mM NH4Cl and 0.5% saponin for 45 min.
Rinse neurons once with buffer A.
Incubate neurons with primary antibodies in buffer A containing 5% NGS and 0.1% saponin for 1 h.
Rinse neurons twice with buffer A, 5 min each.
Incubate neurons with secondary antibodies in buffer A containing 5% NGS and 0.1% saponin for 45 min away from light.
Rinse neurons three times with buffer A, 5 min each.
Postfix neurons with 2% FA in PBS on ice for 10 min.
Warm neurons to 21°C–25°C for an additional 5 min after postfixing.
Rinse neurons three times with PBS containing 50 mM NH4Cl.
Incubate neurons with PBS containing DAPI for 5 min.
Mount coverslips on glass slide with mounting medium after rinsing once with PBS and then with distilled ddH2O.
Open an image with the Fiji-ImageJ software.
Convert image format to 16-bit.
Draw ROI around the dendrite outlined by adjusting the Brightness/Contrast of the fluorescent signals of mCherry the volume marker.
Record ROI from Step C with the ROI Manager.
Measure mean intensity of PI3P in ROI.
Measure mean intensity of Rab8 in ROI.
Record mean intensity of PI3P or Rab8 signals in ROI.
Open an image with the Fiji-ImageJ software.
Convert image format to grayscale images.
Adjust Brightness/Contrast of the fluorescent signals of the volume marker.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) around the dendrite in the mCherry channel with Freehand Selections.
Open ROI Manager.
Press the Add button to select the region specified.
Adjust Designate fluorescence intensity measurement using Set Measurements.
Switch to channel 1 (PI3P) using Channels Tool / Color / Channel 1.
Measure fluorescence mean intensity of PI3P in the dendrite selected previously.
Switch to channel 3 (Rab8) using Channels Tool / Color / Channel 3.
Measure fluorescence mean intensity of Rab8 in ROI.
Transfer data to Excel for analysis.
Analyze the mean intensity of PI3P or Rab8 from more than 10 neurons.
Perform statistical analysis using GraphPad Prism software.
Open an image with NIS-Elements AR software.
Open an image with NIS-Elements software.
Select one channel, e.g., the PI4P channel.
Open LUTs and amplify fluorescence signal to overexposed to identify the background region within the dendrite.
Draw ROI on one or more of the background regions within the dendrite.
View the intensity of PI4P within ROI.
Open an image with the NIS-Elements AR software.
Subtract background using constant.
Draw ROI around plasma membrane of a dendritic segment.
Export data to Excel for further analysis.
Open an image with the NIS-Elements software.
Perform analysis on the 515/30 channel (PI4P signals).
Open LUTs (View / View LUTs).
Amplify fluorescence signal to overexposed so that we can identify the background area within dendrite.
Select a region within dendrite where there is no positive signal using the “area” tool (View / Analysis Controls / Annotations and Measurements / area).
Subtract background using constant to ensure mean intensity of the selected background region < 3. (Image / Background / Subtract Background Using Constant).
Designate fluorescence intensity measurement using Object Features (Measure / Object Features).
Add or remove features for measure as acquired.
Select MeanGreen to measure fluorescence intensity of PM PI4P.
Open Automated Measurement Results (View / Analysis Controls / Automated Measurement Results).
Select ‘Current ROI’ and click ‘Keep updating measurement ON’.
Draw ROI around the PM of a dendritic segment. (Turn ROI On/Off / Draw Polygonal ROI).
Export data generated from “Automated Measurement Results” to Excel.
Analyze mean intensity of PM PI4P from more than 10 neurons.
Perform statistical analysis (t-tests or One-way ANOVA) using the GraphPad Prism software.
